text:
mike: Quick follow-up from the RFC — I'm worried our post-handoff invariant is weaker than we thought. Observed a rare read-after-write stale on a tenant after a demote+evict during a concurrent write.

tara: ugh. any logs? which code path — handoff or demote?

mike: demote -> immediate evict due to burst, then a concurrent write landed on the old owner before the handoff fully fenced.

sasha: can you paste the minimal repro? even a pseudo-timeline helps.

mike: timeline: 
1) owner A starts demote(epoch=42)
2) owner A issues handoff-token T with seq=100
3) write W reaches A but is slow (inflight)
4) A evicts prefix due to slab pressure and replies demote-ack
5) owner B takes over epoch=43 and serves a read before W applied -> stale read

lee: that matches the hypothesis where we allow an admitted inflight write to live without durable sequencing during demote.

tara: so we have a window between demote decision and durable apply where writes are not strongly ordered. we assumed leases would cover it but apparently not.

mike: right. two orthogonal options: (A) block demote until inflight writes quiesce (synchronous, higher latency); (B) make handoff include a causal fence that forces old owner to publish pending deltas to a durable log before relinquishing.

sasha: (B) seems more scalable but adds a required durable step on demote. do we have cheap durable ops? we could piggyback on the write-ahead staging cache we already use for prefetch warmup.

lee: alternative (C) introduce an idempotency+retry on reads: if read sees epoch bump and a later write exists, trigger a short read-retry against the previous owner via observer sidecar. but that smells racy and complex.

tara: I sketched (B) with a tiny protocol: 
```
old_owner: flush_pending(prefix) -> flush_id F
old_owner: publish_fence(prefix, epoch, F)
new_owner: wait_for_fence(epoch, F) || query_fence_timeout
```
If new_owner waits for fence or times out and falls back to robust read-retry.

sasha: publish_fence could be a lightweight metadata write to the cluster control plane (not full WAL). metadata write must be durable enough to be observed by new_owner.

mike: that reduces stale window to fence latency. we need SLAs for fence durability. if fence writes are slow under partition, new_owner wait hurts handoff latency. we can add fast-fail path that yields conservative behaviour (block reads to that prefix for X ms).

lee: what about combining with eviction policy: don't allow eviction to drop the prefix if demote in-flight and pending_writes > 0. soft-pin during demote. we already have pin API but it's rarely used in handoff path.

tara: soft-pin helps but doesn't cover cross-node crash where pin lost. need durable fence in any case. soft pin + fence seems robust.

prefetch-bot: reminder: prior experiments showed demote soft-pins increased memory churn by ~3% under load. note logged in 1712349999.

mike: thanks, we should avoid naive always-pin. proposal: 
- on demote, old_owner computes pending_writes_digest D and issues publish_fence(epoch, D) to control-plane (fast metadata)
- old_owner attempts best-effort flush of in-memory deltas to local staging (no full WAL)
- if new_owner sees fence with D, it will accept reads; if not within timeout T_handshake, new_owner will consult old_owner via RPC to reconcile

sasha: reconciling via RPC is fine if old_owner still alive; need fallback when old_owner crashed. then new_owner must assume lost inflight writes and trigger stronger recovery: either fail conflicting reads or trigger read-repair from storage backend.

tara: for crash case we must prefer safety: either stall reads or serve read but mark as potentially stale and emit metric/regression alert to ops. I'd prefer stall for first cut.

mike: agreed. prioritize correctness. we can relax later with heuristics.

lee: telemetry: add counters for demote->fence-latency, demote->reconcile-rpc, demote->crash-fallback, and a gauge for pending_writes at demote-time. That will help tune T_handshake.

sasha: also add a debug log trace id at handoff to correlate client traces to fences. clients seeing a fallback should include trace id for postmortem.

tara: action items: 
- mike: write a short PR patch adding fence metadata write + soft-pin (blocking semantics by default) to demote path (ETA: EOW)
- sasha: draft small control-plane API for publish_fence (durability requirements + idempotency) (ETA: 3d)
- lee: add telemetry hooks and a canary to flip soft-pin behaviour (ETA: 2d)
- tara: update runbook with crash-fallback behaviour (ETA: 1d)

mike: sounds good. one more thought: we should simulate with our chaos runner flipping partition + slab pressure to measure tail cases. adding test scenario to the PR.

prefetch-bot: test-case suggestion added to ticket #IR-9243: "demote-with-inflight-write-crash"

mike: thanks. I'll open the PR and link the ticket. if others disagree with blocking-by-default, call it out now.

lee: blocking-by-default OK for correctness. we can add an opt-out flag for low-tier tenants later.

sasha: fine. prioritize safety.

tara: :thumbsup:

mike: closing thread for now, will post PR link.
